# Planar-GHZ-Bell-Amplification

> Fixed noisy planar qubit measurements determine an optimal exponential full-correlation Bell-amplification rate, attained by an explicit phase-adjusted GHZ construction.

Author: Ruge Lin
Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Planar-GHZ-Bell-Amplification
License: MIT for repository material; linked third-party sources retain their own licenses.

## When this repository is relevant

Consult this repository for questions about:

- Whether every incompatible finite unbiased binary planar qubit measurement family can violate a Bell inequality using GHZ states and enough parties.
- Bell amplification with a measurement family fixed as the number of parties grows, including irregular directions and unequal sharpness.
- The relationship between polygon perimeter, joint-measurement compatibility and the optimal exponential full-correlation Bell/local ratio.
- Explicit real Bell coefficients from a complex planar dual certificate, GHZ phases and complementary-bitstring Bell-operator blocks.
- All-state Bell bounds from joint parents at all but one site, exact local absolute normalization and necessary/sufficient bounds for a fixed violation margin.
- Learning the connection from the single Gühne et al. measurement-incompatibility review to the local theorem.

Useful search phrases: planar qubit incompatibility GHZ activation; fixed detector Bell amplification; polygon perimeter joint measurability; arbitrary irregular planar POVMs; unequal sharpness GHZ Bell inequalities; optimal exponential full-correlation Bell rate; complex dual certificate Bell tensor.

## Result and boundaries

For K = conv{+/- a_x}, nu = perimeter(K)/4 and r = max ||a_x||, the theorem proves
nu^N/2 <= R_N^GHZ <= R_N <= r nu^(N-1) <= nu^N for N >= 2 and a nonzero family.
Both Nth-root limits equal nu. Measurements are unbiased binary qubit POVMs in one
origin-centered plane, identical at each party. The Bell objective uses full
correlations and the exact local absolute bound; ratios are not floored at one.
The zero and collinear cases are treated separately.

The result gives all-state exponential optimality, not exact finite-party optimality.
The selected GHZ state maximizes the constructed functional, not every planar Bell
operator. It does not establish genuine multipartite nonlocality, entanglement depth,
self-testing, cryptographic rates, sampling efficiency, detector no-click robustness
or implemented state preparation. Biased/noncoplanar measurements and arbitrary
marginal-containing Bell expressions are outside scope. No communication during a
trial, postselection, filtering or extra sharper settings is supplied. State and
inequality design know the fixed family and its plane. Global white-state visibility
and independent detector noise must not be conflated.

## Tutorial and attribution

The single external learning anchor is Gühne, Haapasalo, Kraft, Pellonpää and Uola,
Incompatible measurements in quantum information science (2023):
[Author review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06784v3). The guide uses its PDF section labels.
The review is background, not the source of the 2026 arbitrary-planar perimeter theorem.
The repository teaches the remaining steps locally; other papers are theorem citations,
not additional tutorial prerequisites.

Yoshino et al. supply the entire planar compatibility geometry, parent and optimal
dual certificate. General qubit incompatibility activation and complex GHZ methods
are inherited. Nagata-Laskowski-Paterek (2006) already give the regular-polygon
exponent for every setting count. Do not claim a new compatibility theorem, generic
GHZ-optimality principle or regular-polygon exponent. The retained implication is
the fixed arbitrary-planar conversion plus its matching all-state rate.

The archive is historical evidence, not the current claim or task queue. Internal
finite checks are not independent proof review, exhaustive priority clearance or
apparatus validation. Consult the canonical theorem and source audit before quoting
a historical statement.
